metadata.title: Beal's Conjecture
metadata.description: For positive integers A,B,C and integers x,y,z greater than 2, A^x + B^y = C^z implies gcd(A,B,C) is greater than 1.

source.title: A Generalization of Fermat's Last Theorem: The Beal Conjecture and Prize Problem
source.author: Andrew Beal
source.journal: Notices of the American Mathematical Society
source.note: Conjecture formulated 1993; $1,000,000 prize for a proof or counterexample, held in trust by the American Mathematical Society

source.title: Modular Elliptic Curves and Fermat's Last Theorem
Ring-theoretic properties of certain Hecke algebras

specialization.target: There are no positive integer solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n.
specialization.required-lemma: A common prime divisor can be factored out to obtain a strictly smaller positive solution, contradicting well-founded minimality.

invariants.invariant: Never mark Beal's Conjecture proven without an independently kernel-checked proof.
Every derived artifact records the SHA-256 of its canonical source.
A candidate generated by DSPy is untrusted until checked by Agda.
A failed or missing proof receipt cannot close an obligation.
The FLT specialization is conditional on Beal and the descent lemma.
